title: TMA causes, HELLP & malignant hypertension
guide: HUS, HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, low platelet), the rheumatological pair of catastrophic APS and diffuse scleroderma (Anti RNA P, smaller renal vessels versus Takayasu/PAN in larger vessels), and malignant hypertension = accelerated HTN + papilloedema with new-onset fundal haemorrhage/exudate and emergency HTN at ≥180/120 with end-organ damage.

title: The HUS triangle, the TTP pentagon and the TYPES table
sec: HUS Triad, TTP Pentad & Types · p753
guide: Triangle = thrombocytopenia, renal failure, MAHA; pentagon adds fever, GI symptoms and neurological symptoms (brain). Typical/D+ starts in childhood (<5 y) after dysentery with good prognosis; atypical/D− affects any age, is genetic (m/c) or drug induced, and 50% progress to ESRD with a higher post-transplant recurrence rate.

title: Pathophysiology, typical toxins & the 90% rule
guide: Endothelial damage → VWF release → platelet plug → schistocytes (MAHA) and, through platelets trapped in the plug, thrombocytopenia. Typical/childhood (90%) is toxin driven: Shiga-like/verocytotoxin from EHEC O157:H7 (m/c), Shiga toxin from Shigella dysenteriae and neuraminidase from Streptococcus pneumoniae.

title: Atypical HUS: genetics, drugs & laboratory work-up
sec: Atypical HUS Genetics, Drugs & Investigations · p754
guide: Genetic (m/c) alternate-pathway activation with low C3 and normal C4 — factor H mutation (m/c), factor B (worst prognosis), MCP (best prognosis), factor I. Sporadic drug-induced: mitomycin, gemcitabine, bevacizumab, calcineurin inhibitors, ticlopidine/clopidogrel (TTP also), cisplatin; immune-mediated: quinine, gemcitabine, quetiapine, cotrimoxazole. Smear schistocytes >2%, ↑LDH, ↑indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin, negative Coombs, normal PT/APTT; SLE instead shows classical pathway with low C3 and low C4.

title: Presentation, treatment & the pre-renal/ATN note
sec: Presentation, Treatment & Pre-renal vs ATN · p755
guide: Typical HUS: abdominal pain → 2 days → bloody dysentery (evaluate & start antibiotics) → 5 days → 90–95% resolve, 5–10% HUS; treatment conservative. Atypical: thrombocytopenia with features of secondary hypertension; PLEX within 24h is the mainstay, eculizumab is costly, immunosuppression for factor H mutation, transplant, and rituximab plus eculizumab for post-transplant recurrence. The closing note separates pre-renal injury from acute tubular necrosis on urine output, edema, BUN/creatinine ratio, fluids and tubular injury.
